importance_ranking.reason: Accommodation is a visual trust decision — buyers assess cleanliness, room quality, and property ambience entirely through photos. Absent or poor images cause immediate skip regardless of price or location.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Guest houses are overwhelmingly independent properties with no nationally recognised brand names; buyers choose by location, property name, and reviews rather than brand affinity.
importance_ranking.reason: For accommodation services, the seller IS the product — the property name, location, and operational reputation are what the buyer is purchasing. A buyer cannot separate the service from the provider.

price_display_type.determination_note: Guest house rates vary substantially by room type (AC/non-AC, single/double/suite) and stay duration (daily vs monthly), meaning buyers cannot meaningfully compare prices without knowing the room configuration and stay length.

importance_ranking.reason: Indian travellers and corporate bookers compare per-night rates aggressively across properties; price is a primary shortlisting signal once visual and location fit is confirmed, and India price sensitivity is high in this segment.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Corporate and extended-stay bookings are often quoted per month; the contamination segment (prefab structures) uses per sq ft or per piece — unit must always be shown to prevent price misreading across these contexts.
importance_ranking.reason: Per day vs per month creates genuine price comparison confusion for corporate buyers evaluating extended stays; unit is a necessary qualifier for any price shown on this MCAT.
Room type, AC/non-AC status, and amenities confirm fit after initial visual and price shortlisting — buyers arrive knowing their requirement and use specs to verify, not to discover options.
